title: Valuing dung beetles on Florida cattle ranches
text: RancheR estimates annual economic benefit dung beetles provide cattle operation. Dung beetles break bury dung pats; without , pats sit pasture far longer, fouling grass cattle refuse graze. accelerating pat decay, beetles free grazing area — effectively raising carrying capacity ranch. package turns ecological service dollars, using empirical pat-decay data Central Florida pasture research (Stanbrook-Buyer, Bhat & King, 2024). contains calculations power RancheR Shiny app, exposed plain R functions can script , batch , build tools top.

title: Valuing dung beetles on Florida cattle ranches
text: calculation follows four steps: Decay rate. beetle-abundance scenario empirical pat decay rate (grams/day). beetles → faster decay. Fouled pasture. Faster decay means fewer grazing-area units (GAU) pasture fouled per cow per year. package stores empirically measured fouled area scenario. Avoided fouling. Comparing scenario -beetle baseline gives GAU fouling avoided thanks beetles. Dollar value. Avoided fouling converted equivalent number additional cows freed pasture can support, multiplied ranch-level income per cow.

title: Valuing dung beetles on Florida cattle ranches
text: main function calc_dung_beetle_benefit(). argument must supply herd size; everything else sensible paper-derived default. return value list. two headline numbers usually:
code: res <- calc_dung_beetle_benefit(   num_cattle = 100,   scenario   = "Managed (low beetle abundance)" )  res #> $annual_value #> [1] 454.8576 #>  #> $additional_cows #> [1] 0.5601695 #>  #> $days_to_decay #> [1] 112.61 #>  #> $decay_rate #> [1] 7.23 #>  #> $fouled_used #> [1] 31820 #>  #> $avoided_gau_per_cow #> [1] 20272 #>  #> $climate_factor #> [1] 1 res$annual_value     # estimated annual benefit, in dollars #> [1] 454.8576 res$additional_cows  # equivalent extra cows the freed pasture supports #> [1] 0.5601695

title: Valuing dung beetles on Florida cattle ranches
text: three beetle-abundance scenarios. can list dung_scenarios(): decay rates (grams dung removed per day) : beetles remove dung faster, economic benefit rises “beetles” baseline “natural” high-abundance case. benefit 100-head operation scenario: “beetles” scenario baseline, avoided fouling — therefore benefit — zero construction.
code: dung_scenarios() #> [1] "No beetles (low decay rate)"     "Managed (low beetle abundance)"  #> [3] "Natural (high beetle abundance)" sapply(dung_scenarios(), scenario_decay_rate) #>     No beetles (low decay rate)  Managed (low beetle abundance)  #>                            3.75                            7.23  #> Natural (high beetle abundance)  #>                           10.73 herd <- 100 benefits <- sapply(dung_scenarios(), function(s) {   calc_dung_beetle_benefit(num_cattle = herd, scenario = s)$annual_value })  data.frame(   scenario     = dung_scenarios(),   annual_value = round(benefits, 2),   row.names    = NULL ) #>                          scenario annual_value #> 1     No beetles (low decay rate)         0.00 #> 2  Managed (low beetle abundance)       454.86 #> 3 Natural (high beetle abundance)       673.74

what: Adjusting decay rates for your own climate
title: Valuing dung beetles on Florida cattle ranches
text: decay rates measured single Central Florida site (27.1301368, -81.1978989) summer, temperature rainfall strongly drive dung decomposition. Decay slower cooler drier regions faster hotter, wetter ones, ranch elsewhere needs locally adjusted rates. estimate_local_decay() scaling reference rates location’s climate differs Florida site. Climate comes two WorldClim “bioclim” variables chosen match summer collection window: BIO10 — mean temperature warmest quarter (°C) BIO18 — precipitation warmest quarter (mm) Temperature acts Q10 response (decay changes factor q10, default 2, per 10 °C — standard description biological decomposition), moisture saturating response (decay rises rainfall diminishing returns). normalised 1 reference climate, model reproduces measured rates exactly Florida site. note method. decay measured one location, calibrated, literature-grounded scaling — regression fitted multi-site data. q10 precip_half_sat arguments exposed relationship can tuned replaced local field data become available.

title: Valuing dung beetles on Florida cattle ranches
text: Applied geographically, model gives decay rate ranch. map places handful sites labels estimated managed-scenario rate (g/day). warmest-quarter climate values illustrative approximations demonstration — practice estimate_local_decay(lat, lon) looks real WorldClim values .
code: sites <- data.frame(   name            = c("FL reference", "S. Texas", "Georgia", "Wisconsin", "Colorado"),   lon             = c(-81.20, -98.49, -83.40, -89.50, -105.00),   lat             = c( 27.13,  27.80,  32.80,  44.00,   40.30),   temp_warmq_C    = c( 27.31,  29.50,  26.80,  20.30,   17.50),   precip_warmq_mm = c(   522,    210,    330,    290,     140) )  sites$decay_managed <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(sites)), function(i) {   estimate_local_decay(     lat = sites$lat[i], lon = sites$lon[i],     climate = c(temp_warmq_C = sites$temp_warmq_C[i],                 precip_warmq_mm = sites$precip_warmq_mm[i])   )$decay_rates[["Managed (low beetle abundance)"]] }, numeric(1))  pal  <- hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE) cols <- pal[cut(sites$decay_managed, breaks = 100, labels = FALSE)]  maps::map("state", fill = TRUE, col = "grey95", border = "grey80") points(sites$lon, sites$lat, pch = 21, bg = cols, cex = 2.4) text(sites$lon, sites$lat, sprintf("%.1f", sites$decay_managed),      pos = 3, cex = 0.75) title("Estimated managed-scenario decay rate (g/day)")

title: Estimate the annual economic benefit of dung beetles to a ranch — calc_dung_beetle_benefit
text: num_cattle Number cattle operation. scenario Dung beetle abundance scenario; one dung_scenarios(). Defaults "Managed (low beetle abundance)". pat_weight_g Initial dung pat weight grams. decay_override Optional custom decay rate (g/day). Leave NA use scenario default. supplied, fouled-area scaled -beetle baseline rather read empirical table. income_per_cow Ranch-level income per cow ($/yr). acre_per_cow Acres required per cow per year. climate_factor Climate scaling factor location, returned estimate_local_decay() ($climate_factor). Slower decay (factor 1, e.g. cooler/drier sites) means -beetle baseline beetle scenarios foul pasture proportionally longer, avoided fouling - therefore dollar benefit - scales 1 / climate_factor. Defaults 1 (Central Florida reference climate). Use , empirical scenario path, get location-adjusted benefit; composes correctly climate model whereas decay_override .

title: Climate scaling factor for dung decay — climate_decay_factor
text: temp_C Mean temperature warmest quarter target location (deg C; WorldClim BIO10). precip_mm Precipitation warmest quarter target location (mm; WorldClim BIO18). q10 Temperature sensitivity: factor decay changes per 10 deg C. Defaults 2.0, typical value biological decomposition. precip_half_sat Half-saturation constant moisture response (mm). Larger values make decay less sensitive rainfall. Defaults reference site's warmest-quarter precipitation. ref_temp_C, ref_precip_mm Reference-site climate factor normalised . Defaults calibration values rancher_constants.

text: named list elements: initial_pat_g Initial dung pat weight (grams). decay_no_beetles Pat decay rate beetles (g/day). decay_managed Pat decay rate, managed / low beetle abundance (g/day). decay_natural Pat decay rate, natural / high beetle abundance (g/day). income_per_cow Ranch-level income per cow ($/yr). acre_per_cow Acres required per cow per year. gau_per_acre Grazing-area units per acre (m^2 per acre). fouled_gau_per_cow_year Named vector empirically fouled GAU per cow per year, scenario. ref_lat, ref_lon Latitude/longitude Central Florida site decay rates measured. ref_temp_warmq_C WorldClim BIO10 (mean temperature warmest quarter, deg C) reference site; temperature anchor climate scaling. ref_precip_warmq_mm WorldClim BIO18 (precipitation warmest quarter, mm) reference site; moisture anchor climate scaling.
